quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When daylight fades, what should you use so others can see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight begins to fade. Use high beams only in empty areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do before you start your car?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt before starting the car. Also make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: You have a minor accident at an intersection with no injuries or serious damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
questions.explanation: After an accident with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on roads and highways?

options.text: No passing allowed.
Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you are ready to turn right?

options.text: Signal and turn right away.
Stop before the right lane and wait for all traffic to pass.
Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Reduce your speed and stop at the limit line if needed. Then make your turn.

questions.question: Why should you keep signaling while you turn?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal during a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Turning off your signal during a turn is always unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, cyclists, and pedestrians your intentions.

questions.question: What happens if you pass a stopped school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: You can be fined up to $1,000.
You can be fined up to $100.
There are no legal consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be fined up to $1,000.
questions.explanation: You must stop when you see a school bus with red lights flashing. If you don't stop, you can lose your license and be fined up to $1,000.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Drive at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: Which child needs a child passenger restraint system?

options.text: A 9-year-old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall
A 10-year-old who is 5 feet 3 inches tall
A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall

questions.correctAnswerText: A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall
questions.explanation: Children 8 years or older or at least 4 feet 9 inches tall may use a safety belt. All other children must use a child passenger restraint system.

questions.question: What can happen if you abandon an animal on the highway?

options.text: You can go to jail.
You get a point on your license.
Nothing happens legally.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go to jail.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to dump or leave an animal on the highway. You can face up to six months in jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Drive to the right edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes move in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road widens ahead.
One lane ends soon. Merge left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane ends soon. Merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a lane is ending and traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: When you drive through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Drive through carefully and do not slow down to look around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully and do not slow down to look around.
questions.explanation: Do not "rubberneck" or slow down to look at unusual things. This causes traffic problems.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians before entering an intersection. Look left again since vehicles from the left are closer. Check across the intersection to make sure the path is clear.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep scanning ahead for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning ahead for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead for hazards. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow down to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Why should you look for bicyclists in the same lanes used by motor vehicles?

options.text: They must ride facing oncoming traffic.
They illegally share lanes with motor vehicles.
They have the right to use the road with motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have the right to use the road with motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the legal right to use the road. They may ride on certain parts of freeways where there is no other route and bicycling is allowed. Watch for bicyclists and share the road with them.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, wait to cross until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Treat it like a stop sign.
Stop and yield to all traffic before crossing.
Slow down and be alert before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be alert before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution. Slow down and be alert. Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles in the intersection. You do not have to stop.

questions.question: A traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic laws, signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: At an intersection if there are no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and road markings permit passing.
Around a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings permit passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass at intersections or near parking lot entrances. If a curve or hill blocks your view, stay in your lane and assume a vehicle is coming. Only pass where signs and markings allow it, and only if you have enough safe space.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three.
Two.
One.

questions.correctAnswerText: One.
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downgrade ahead. Check your brakes before going down.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop. Look far ahead to give yourself time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car more visible. If you use windshield wipers, you must also use low beam headlights.

questions.question: When you tailgate (drive very close behind another vehicle), what happens?

options.text: You can anger and frustrate other drivers.
You cannot get a traffic ticket for it.
You help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can anger and frustrate other drivers.
questions.explanation: Most rear-end crashes happen because of tailgating. Use the Three Second Rule: count three seconds from when the car ahead passes a point until you reach it. If you reach it sooner, you are too close.

questions.question: When passing a car, you have enough space to return to your lane when:

options.text: The other driver signals you to come back.
You look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
You can see both of the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both of the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe gap between your vehicle and the passed car before returning to your lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down mechanically, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, get it off the road away from traffic if possible. Turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers know you are having trouble.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass when you are sure you can change lanes safely. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you try to pass.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to regain traction.
Press the brakes hard to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, your tires can ride on a layer of water above the road. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep the dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.
